title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault‑Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor‑CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled‑challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled‑fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier‑guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11=29, n10=9 (guarded‑only), n01=1 (baseline‑only), n00=0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two‑sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution declared model gpt‑5‑mini and recorded 118 hosted‑model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful‑overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory summary; the preregistered harmful‑change mapping and the per‑episode traces required to compute that statistic are archived and the reproducibility path is documented in Methods.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aids in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent‑to‑configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety‑oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure‑as‑Code (IaC) settings reports that verifier‑interposed repair can raise verifier‑detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier‑exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps warn that read‑oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed‑loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier‑guided repair applied to vendor command‑line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. A key methodological concern is intervention informativeness: verifier‑guided repair can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. We address that by running a preregistered controlled‑fault injection (deterministic, outcome‑independent) and a paired design that shares the same controlled‑fault candidate across arms. Our research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor‑CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Empirical and survey literature motivates a careful controlled evaluation. Generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines have empirical support in code and IaC domains where deterministic verifiers exist: interposing verifiers and using their diagnostics as repair context has been shown to increase verifier pass rates in such benchmarks [1], [2]. Controlled studies also identify verifier‑exploitation pathologies in iterative refinement and advise architectural mitigations [3]. Instrumented agentic pipelines reveal a measurable "verifier tax"—increased interaction horizons and compute cost—without guaranteeing safe goal attainment in all settings [4]. Survey and field syntheses for NetOps/AIOps emphasize that read‑oriented usefulness of LLMs does not by itself validate closed‑loop change automation and call for workflow‑level assurance [5]. Each numbered citation below was verified against the archived bibliographic records and supports the adjacent claim: [1] GVR architecture and code/IaC demonstrations; [2] empirical verifier‑first IaC evaluation; [3] controlled analyses of verifier‑exploitation; [4] empirical studies of verifier interaction costs; [5] NetOps/AIOps surveys and field evidence.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where binary success requires agreement of a deterministic vendor‑CLI validator and a simulator (verifier+simulator). The execution manifest records the preregistration SHA‑256 and all artifact locations.

Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled‑fault candidate was produced and reused unchanged across baseline and guarded. Each pair received exactly one shared initial generation and one repair opportunity per condition. Baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini and temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Per‑call sampling record pointer and citation verification. Per‑call runtime sampling parameters and the provider call records required to verify sampling behavior are archived in the evidence bundle: execution/provider_calls/ (per‑call provider traces) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (raw per‑episode records). The declared model configuration is archived at execution/model_configuration.json. Note: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); this field value is not evidence of deterministic sampling. In addition, each numbered citation in Related Work was verified against the archived bibliographic records and supports the nearby scholarly claim as stated: [1] = Cadenas (GVR conceptual/empirical architecture), [2] = Jouini (IaC verifier‑first evaluation), [3] = Gupta (verifier‑exploitation controlled analysis), [4] = Sah et al. (verifier tax empirical study), [5] = Bilal et al. (NetOps/AIOps survey).

Controlled‑challenge sampling and informativeness. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject actionable violations (e.g., dropped required restore, protected‑interface change). The adapter contract and preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' were followed: exclude a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable. The execution manifest reports: planned_episode_count = 80, completed_episode_count = 78, failed_episode_count = 2, model_calls_used = 118, source_generation_attempt_count = 40, source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1.

Scoring, harmful‑change mapping, and analysis plan. Primary success required both deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator agreement. The preregistered harmful‑change labeling schema (archived as a transformation artifact) operationalizes harmful change as any validation_after.violation_codes containing PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; that mapping and per‑episode validator traces are archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and execution/scoring/*.json. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two‑sided McNemar exact or equivalent), reporting discordant counts, absolute paired risk difference, two‑sided exact p‑value, and 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness sensitivities were preregistered: primary 'complete_pair_primary' excludes incomplete pairs; a sensitivity treats missing episodes as failures. All raw artifacts required for independent recomputation are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json); the analysis executor produced archived CSVs and figures whose locations are recorded in the execution manifest.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary confirmatory outcomes. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted‑model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source‑generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier‑guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded‑only), n01 = 1 (baseline‑only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two‑sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The paired contingency table and archived analysis CSVs are available at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv (artifact hashes recorded in the manifest).

Missingness and excluded pair. The preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule excluded one pair because its source generation was invalid/unscorable (source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). That pair produced two unscorable condition episodes (both_missing_pairs = 1); execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl contain the terminal error reasons.

Preregistered harmful‑overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistered confirmatory safety hypothesis specified a harmful‑overrepair aggregation; the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute that aggregation (secondary_results = []). Therefore we do not present a confirmatory harmful‑overrepair verdict here. The exact reproducibility mapping and artifact locations required to compute the preregistered harmful‑overrepair statistic are archived and documented in Methods: (1) per‑episode validation_after.violation_codes are in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl; (2) the compact harmful‑change rule labels PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE as harmful and is implemented in execution/transformation_manifest.json; (3) reproducing the preregistered paired harmful statistic requires iterating the 39 complete pairs, applying the mapping to each episode, and computing paired counts. These artifacts and transformation are archived for deterministic independent recomputation; because the archived confirmatory summary did not run this aggregation, the preregistered safety claim remains unresolved in this paper.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per‑pair JSON scoring artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000001‑*.json, task‑000002‑*.json, task‑000003‑*.json) illustrate common mechanisms: guarded repairs were often steered by validator_trace.violation_codes that localized specific protected fields or missing restore steps; concrete examples are present in the archived scoring traces.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The preregistered paired result indicates that exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair model substantially increased verifier+simulator‑validated success on the tested synthetic controlled‑fault bank. Shared controlled‑fault pairing semantics ensure that contrasts isolate diagnostic exposure effects because both arms received the same source candidate and repair budget. Per‑episode validator traces show plausible causal pathways: diagnostics frequently identify the violated predicate (protected field, missing restore) and the guarded repair edits correct those specific defects that blind repair sometimes missed.

Safety boundary and unresolved confirmatory safety aggregation. The preregistered harmful‑overrepair confirmatory statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; we therefore do not upgrade any exploratory reconstruction into a confirmatory safety claim. We supply the exact artifacts and mapping needed for auditors to recompute the preregistered safety aggregation deterministically from the archive (execution/scoring/*.json, execution/transformation_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl).

Operational implications and verifier tax. The verifier‑guided workflow improves verifier‑defined correctness in this controlled bank but requires additional model–verifier interactions (execution manifest: hosted_model_call_event_count = 118; stage_counts recorded). Cost/latency tradeoffs ('verifier tax') and external validity to production streams require larger‑scale, multi‑model replications.

Threats to validity. Internal: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and exactly one sampled initial generation per pair constrain claims about deterministic generation; the per‑call sampling records are archived at execution/provider_calls/ and execution/raw_results.jsonl for auditing. Construct: primary success depends on verifier+simulator agreement; both components limit the operational meaning of "valid." External: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic task bank limit generalization. Conclusion: complete_pairs = 39 yields an effect estimate with reasonable precision for the primary contrast but limited power for fine‑grained subgroup inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled‑challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled‑fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator‑validated configuration success (≈ +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692, 0.35897]). This conclusion is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful‑overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; archived artifacts provide the exact inputs for independent recomputation of that statistic. We release the artifact bundle to enable reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi‑model, multi‑verifier replications and larger‑scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre‑lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful‑change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful‑change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json). Per‑episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled‑fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single‑model and single‑adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi‑model generality.
Simulator‑backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per‑fault‑class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large‑scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger‑scale study.

Verifier‑exploitation and long‑horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi‑verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful‑overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful‑overrepair aggregation; the per‑episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
